claims.text: Controlled Pd incorporation into NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloys narrows the distribution of local exchange interaction energies.
Pd incorporation produces a more magnetically homogeneous alloy.
The Pd-induced magnetic homogenization facilitates a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields.
Pd-induced magnetic homogenization minimizes magnetic hysteresis.
Pd incorporation preserves rapid heat exchange.
Pd incorporation preserves mechanical integrity.
A NiFeCoCr alloy with minimal or no Pd has a broader exchange-energy distribution than Pd-containing or heat-treated variants.
The proposed intervention reduces compositional disorder and increases microstructural homogeneity.
The narrowed exchange-energy distribution mediates a balance between magnetic-domain uniformity and domain-wall mobility.
A more uniform magnetic-domain structure lowers energy barriers for domain reorientation.
Lower domain-reorientation barriers reduce magnetic hysteresis.
Lower domain-reorientation barriers enable a large, reversible magnetocaloric effect at low fields.
The Pd-induced microstructural adjustments maintain efficient thermal pathways.
Controlled Pd additions will enhance magnetocaloric entropy change at low magnetic fields relative to minimally Pd-doped NiFeCoCr.
Controlled Pd additions will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the baseline.
Controlled Pd additions will not deteriorate heat-exchange rates relative to the baseline.
Controlled Pd additions will not deteriorate mechanical strength relative to the baseline.
The minimally Pd-doped baseline has higher hysteresis losses than controlled-Pd variants.
The minimally Pd-doped baseline has a less pronounced low-field magnetocaloric response than controlled-Pd variants.
Above the moderate-addition or processing range, secondary phases may form and alter magnetic or mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The intervention says Pd can be added through post-synthesis heat treatment, but heat treatment alone can redistribute existing constituents and alter exchange-energy distributions; it cannot incorporate Pd unless an additional deposition, diffusion, or alloying step is specified.
